audience.programmeDescription: Leiden Computer Science combines programming and software with algorithms, mathematical foundations, computer systems, data and artificial intelligence. The degree develops practical and theoretical problem solving and concludes with an individual research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers a qualified composition in computer science, data and intelligent systems. It combines software, algorithms, databases, networks and operating systems with mathematics, statistical research and substantial AI study. It does not reproduce the dedicated digital-hardware, computer-architecture and technical-security sequence, or the compulsory Leiden thesis. The data and AI content is integrated into this composition rather than presented again as a separate option.

curriculum.limitation: Years one and two each contain 60 EC of required study. Year three contains 30 EC of open choice, a selected 6-EC advanced option, AI and Ethics (3 EC), Software Engineering (6 EC) and the thesis project (15 EC). Computer Graphics is the illustrated advanced option and requires fluent C/C++ programming and attendance. Its autumn placement alongside 30 EC of open choice gives 36 EC in autumn and 24 EC in spring. The thesis includes a compulsory bachelor class and matching in November–December. By 1 February, students need the full 60-EC first year, at least 66 EC from years two and three, completed Research Methods, and no more than 27 EC of outstanding upper-year spring courses excluding the thesis; a September precheck also applies. It includes a proposal, peer review, progress presentation, draft review, final report and presentation under LIACS supervision and a second assessor. Open choice can use an eligible Leiden–Delft–Rotterdam minor or five CS electives; other packages require approval and overlapping content must be replaced.

componentNotes.y3-elective-space: 30 EC of genuine open choice, subject to applicable approval and overlap rules.
componentNotes.y3-computer-graphics: Selected 6-EC advanced option in 3D computer graphics, including C/C++ practical work.
componentNotes.y3-thesis: 15 EC of individual research with compulsory bachelor-class participation and applicable entry requirements.

selectedDescriptions.name: Personal & Professional Development
selectedDescriptions.description: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

selectedDescriptions.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
selectedDescriptions.description: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

selectedDescriptions.name: Research Methods & Statistics
selectedDescriptions.description: Research Methods & Statistics introduces research design, operationalisation, measurement, sampling, surveys and experiments. Students study descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression using R and R Commander. A group project develops a research plan and instruments, collects and analyses data, and reports findings under research-ethics and privacy requirements.

selectedDescriptions.name: AI Ethics
selectedDescriptions.description: AI Ethics examines artificial intelligence from philosophical and psychological perspectives. Topics include fairness, privacy, responsibility, human-value alignment, moral status and political or existential risks. Students apply ethical frameworks to questions about human behaviour and interaction, synthesise research in an analytical psychology project, and produce a research-based podcast.

selectedDescriptions.name: Decision-making in AI
selectedDescriptions.description: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Students study probability, Bayesian networks, temporal models, expected utility, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

selectedDescriptions.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
selectedDescriptions.description: Introduces formal logic, abstract reasoning and proof. Students work with propositions, quantified statements, sets, Boolean algebra, functions and relations, direct and indirect proofs, induction and recursion. A final component models processes and games without chance and investigates winning strategies.

selectedDescriptions.description: Optimization Methods in AI studies search and optimisation for rational agents. Topics include uninformed and heuristic search, local and global optimisation, adversarial search, constraint satisfaction, linear programming and discrete optimisation. Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.

selectedDescriptions.description: Image Processing & Computer Vision studies how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognise structures and objects. Topics include colour, image statistics, filtering, segmentation, feature detection, tracking and object classification. Practical work uses Python and OpenCV to develop and benchmark an image-recognition pipeline on previously unseen images.
